source_text.ISS-0932: id: ISS-0932 (queue Q-915, GH-2066); title: D3: Regulatory Compliance Review definition lacks the 21-day timer path to BaFin escalation; severity MAJOR; discovered_by UAT-RUNNER (ISS-0912 QA re-run 2026-10-01). Symptom: POST /instances/:id/advance-timer on risk-evaluation returns 404; regulatory-auto-escalation only reachable from the post-remediation-check unresolved branch. Evidence test/uat-reports/uat-2026-10-01-ISS0912-NARRATIVE.yaml (D3). Scenario test/fixtures/uat/scenarios/meridian/regulatory-compliance-review-bafin.yaml. Definition fixture test/fixtures/qa/meridian_regulatory_compliance_review_process_definition.json. ORCH findings (verify): risk-evaluation is HUMAN_TASK with only {role}; no pending timer exists so advance-timer 404s (Scheduler.resolve_advance_target picks the single pending timer, 400 if >1, 404 if none); edge timeout-risk-evaluation goes risk-evaluation->risk-evaluation-timeout->severity-routing->findings-sign-off, never regulatory-auto-escalation; HUMAN_TASK escalation_timer_duration only reassigns role; a :TIMER node (duration_iso8601) is the engine's routable timer. Required outcome: after evidence-collection completes a pending P21D timer exists, advance-timer fires it, flow runs regulatory-auto-escalation (SERVICE_TASK POST .../compliance/regulatory-notice) -> end-closed, instance COMPLETED; normal path (risk manager completes risk-evaluation -> severity-routing ...) must keep working with no dangling timer trouble. Consider whether reason 'sla_breach_30_days' must be in the service-task body. No QA data/DB changes; repo fixtures/definitions/tests/docs only; bump fixture version if appropriate.

result.summary: Independent verification of lib/letflow/design/q915-regulatory-review-21day-timer-path.md. Re-executed a scratch script (not committed) applying the design to the real fixture: Graph.validate_graph / validate_node_attributes / validate_edge_conditions all valid with no violations; Transition.transition/3 complete_task -> severity-routing for vars %{}, low, critical (so e3 constant-true does not change normal-path behaviour and does not silently escalate); escalation_timer_fired -> regulatory-auto-escalation for all three variable sets. Code reads confirmed: really_conditioned?/1 (transition.ex:566), advance_off_completed_node (conditioned first, then first non-conditioned default) and dispatch_escalation_timer_fired (skips conditioned, takes first default) so e3 is skipped on the timer path; dispatch_human_task arms :escalation_timer_armed when escalation_timer_duration is non-empty binary and engine.ex:696/716 consumes it; resolve_advance_target(nil) returns single pending timer / :no_pending_timer; router calls resolve_advance_target then fire_timer; fire_timer/2 and advance_after_service_task_outcome/4 signatures match the E1 steps; helpers named in the test spec exist in engine_catalog_service_task_test.exs. Current fixture matches the design's 'old' column (v1.1, risk-evaluation role-only, e4 and risk-evaluation-timeout present, YAML has same nodes/edges). All issue outcomes covered (timer exists after evidence-collection, advance-timer fires it, regulatory-auto-escalation -> end-closed COMPLETED via E1, normal path via T10/T11/E2). Tests are runnable (pure Transition + DB harness cited), fail-first expectations are consistent with the old shape, and mutations M1-M10 map to discriminating assertions. No implementation code in the design (tables/prose only); lib/ unchanged and justified. Not run: the two specified test files do not exist yet (design-only gate); E1 DB steps verified by code reading, not execution.
